subfiles.title: Army request for concurrence in Far Eastern potash procurement
subfiles.from: John P. Loomis, Deputy Food Administrator for Occupied Areas, Department of the Army
subfiles.to: Chief, International Resources Division, Department of State, attention C. W. Nichols
subfiles.about: The Army requests expedited State Department approval to purchase the balance of the minimum potash requirements for Japan, the Ryukyus, and Korea from Eastern Germany and possibly Spain.
subfiles.summary: Loomis details Army plans to meet Far East potash needs of 245,400 tons via contracts with Spain, Germany, and others, seeking quick concurrence before offers expire.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on German and Spanish potash purchases
subfiles.from: C. W. Nichols, Assistant Chief, International Resources Division, Department of State
subfiles.to: John P. Loomis, Deputy Food Administrator for Occupied Areas, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: The State Department approves additional procurement from Germany but declines to approve further purchases from Spain pending examination of their effect on Dutch and other European supplies.
subfiles.summary: Nichols approves German potash purchases for the Far East but declines further Spanish purchases, to protect Dutch access to Spain's supply.

interest: Shows 1948 US coordination to supply potash fertilizer to occupied Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus from multiple countries.
